By trade, I'm a historian of [early modern](https://sharonhoward.org/earlymodern.html) Britain and a digital historian, and I've been project manager/researcher on many [digital history projects](https://sharonhoward.org/projects.html). 

I like playing with historical datasets, wrangling messy data and writing code, mostly R. This blog is a playground and a resource, where I want to bring together digital history and data science while working on better code. I'm working on getting better at Javascript for interactive visualisations. 

Wherever possible, data will be publicly available. Unless otherwise stated, code/visualisations are licensed under a [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) 

The site is built using the [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) publishing system.

[Sharon Howard](https://sharonhoward.org)
